rows.subtype: Approach: noticing warning signs and taking them seriously [Thinking]
rows.description: A teen sees a friend withdraw, stop eating lunch and say things like nothing matters, and decides these changes are serious enough to act on rather than something he should just wait out.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, mental simulation

rows.subtype: Approach: listening without judging and staying connected [Action]
rows.description: A student sits with her friend, listens without lecturing, asks how she is really doing, and tells her she matters, aiming to be present while not pretending to be a therapist.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, mental simulation

rows.subtype: Approach: involving a trusted adult even against a request for secrecy [Action]
rows.description: Though the friend begs him to keep quiet, a teen tells the school counsellor and his own parent, reasoning that a friend's safety outweighs a promise and that adults can arrange proper help.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, mental simulation

rows.subtype: Approach: using helplines and emergency services when danger is immediate [Action]
rows.description: If a friend is in immediate danger, a teen knows to call a family adult and the emergency number or a mental health helpline at once rather than handling it alone.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, mental simulation

rows.subtype: Approach: trying to fix everything alone [Pitfall]
rows.description: A student becomes his friend's only support, answers messages through the night and hides how bad it is, until his own sleep and marks collapse and the friend still has no professional help.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: mental simulation

rows.subtype: Approach: dismissing it as attention seeking [Pitfall]
rows.description: A teen tells herself her friend is exaggerating and changes the subject, missing a real chance to connect her with help and leaving the friend feeling more alone.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, mental simulation

rows.subtype: Approach: keeping the secret to protect the friendship [Pitfall]
rows.description: A student fears losing trust if he tells anyone, so he keeps the friend's distress secret for weeks, carrying a burden too heavy for a teenager and delaying real care.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, mental simulation

rows.subtype: Approach: caring for own limits and feelings [Revision]
rows.description: After several heavy conversations, a teen notices she is exhausted and anxious, talks to her mother about it, and agrees to share the support with adults, keeping a friendly role only.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, mental simulation

rows.subtype: Approach: following up after the first conversation [Revision]
rows.description: A teen checks in the next day and again the next week, invites his friend for a walk, and adjusts by involving the friend's family when the friend still seems to be struggling.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, mental simulation

rows.description: Before approaching a struggling friend, a student plans simple words such as I have noticed you seem low and I am worried about you, and what to do if the friend gets angry or shuts down.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination
